findings.title: AC4 computed pair total not stated in MR
findings.problem: AC4 requires the baseline to hold all 16 hand-reproduced pairs and the computed total to be stated in the MR. The 16 pairs are enforced by test_baseline_contains_hand_reproduced_pairs, and route_precedence.json holds 45 entries (verified: 227 lines, 5 per entry plus brackets). The 45-pair total appears only in the implementation notes and regenerate_baselines output, not in any MR-bound text; the acceptance lens graded the criterion partial.
findings.impact: A story acceptance criterion stays partially met: the MR reviewer cannot see how many order-dependent pairs the guard pins, against the 40 pairs the ticket's static scan estimated.
findings.recommendation: State the computed total (45 overlapping route pairs, versus the ticket's 40 static-scan estimate) in the MR description and record that text as the evidence artifact mapped to CR-001 for the check round.

findings.title: MCP auth routers outside guarded profile
findings.problem: PROFILE_ENV sets "MCP_AUTH_ENABLED": "false" (guarded_app.py:55-56), so get_mcp_auth_router() and get_cimd_router() (main.py:1099-1100) return the 503 stub routers (src/codemie/enterprise/mcp_auth/router.py:522-531). The enabled_router and enabled_cimd_router routes (for example GET /v1/mcp-auth/oauth2/callback-page.js and the 200 variant of GET /v1/mcp-auth/status) and their schemas are in neither the OpenAPI snapshot nor the precedence baseline, while the module docstring (guarded_app.py:22) says "Every conditional router of ``main.py`` is on".
findings.impact: The guard's stated coverage is false. These routers are registered last and are outside the five packages being split, so no regression is expected from the split itself, but whether a later step can affect them was not established (reachability of that consequence unconfirmed).
findings.recommendation: Either enable MCP auth in the hermetic profile (regenerate both baselines and assert an enabled-only route in test_guarded_app_profile.py), or keep it off and correct the docstring to name the MCP auth enabled variants as an intentional, recorded gap.

findings.title: Probe failure re-spawns per test; timeout drops stderr
findings.problem: load_guarded_app_dump is decorated with @functools.cache (guarded_app.py:71), which stores only successful returns. subprocess.run(..., timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) (lines 76-83, 180 s) has no except subprocess.TimeoutExpired, and only the non-zero-exit branch (lines 84-85) puts result.stderr in its error. A failing or hanging import of main.py therefore re-runs the probe for each consuming test (test_openapi_snapshot, the precedence tests, the module-scoped profile fixture), and a timeout surfaces without the child's stderr.
findings.impact: On a loaded or broken CI runner a hung probe costs up to 180 s per consuming test before failing, which can exhaust the job timeout and lose the pytest report, and the stalled import cannot be diagnosed. The guard still fails rather than passing, so this is a failure-path robustness gap.
findings.recommendation: Cache the failure so later calls re-raise the same RuntimeError, and catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired to raise a RuntimeError that includes the child's captured stderr (exc.stderr).

findings.title: Bare dict return annotations in new tests
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports, line 19) lists bare dict annotations under Avoid and prefers parameterized generics. New code has three: test_guarded_app_profile.py:25 `def dump() -> dict:`, test_route_overlap.py:45 and test_route_precedence.py:96, both `def _route(path: str, *methods: str) -> dict:`.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is broken in new code, and the standards review marks it blocking for the workflow.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the annotations: `-> dict[str, Any]` for dump() (it holds openapi, routes and contacts_attempted) and `-> dict[str, object]` for both _route() helpers; import Any in test_guarded_app_profile.py.
